title: getPartnerForUser/getEmployerForUser upsert default-org preview rows and can open any first employer
blast: A super_admin with no impersonation cookie who opens /partner or /employer triggers ensureSuperAdminFallbackPartner / ensureSuperAdminFallbackEmployer: partner.upsert slug workforce-solutions-austin and user.upsert email employer-preview@example.com into getDefaultOrganizationId(). If that fails, findFirst any active partner/employer (orderBy createdAt asc) — so the first row in the table, any tenant, becomes the portal context. That is a cross-tenant PII view (candidate emails, applications) created as a side effect of navigation. Cookie setter is httpOnly UUID, not HMAC-signed (unlike MFA trust).
evidence: lib/auth/roles.ts:326-345 ensureSuperAdminFallbackPartner upserts into getDefaultOrganizationId(). :348-385 ensureSuperAdminFallbackEmployer upserts preview user+employer. :200-228 getPartnerForUser falls through to anyActivePartner. :438-452 getEmployerForUser falls through to anyActiveEmployer. app/api/admin/employer-context/route.ts:16-22 cookie is httpOnly UUID, no signature. Contrast lib/auth/mfaTrust.ts:15-20 HMAC required.

title: Apply signup always writes users/applications into getDefaultOrganizationId()
blast: Sibling of clm_secrets_orphan_user_default_org (healer). The conversion path itself never consults resolveOrgFromRequest / custom-domain x-wap-org-id. app/api/apply/signup/route.ts:367 organizationId = getDefaultOrganizationId() then user + application + profile creates use that id. A custom-domain school funnel still stamps workforceap. First beat mapped only the healer; this is the write that creates the row the healer later 'heals'. Tests mock getDefaultOrganizationId and never assert request-org.
evidence: app/api/apply/signup/route.ts:13 import getDefaultOrganizationId; :367 const organizationId = await withDbRetry(() => getDefaultOrganizationId()); :406,:437,:575 create payloads include that organizationId. No resolveOrgFromRequest in the file. app/api/apply/signup/route.test.ts mocks getDefaultOrganizationId → org-test-1.

title: Admin APIs are often tenant-scoped; matching SSR pages still list every tenant
blast: Deep pass walked app/admin/**/page.tsx vs app/api/admin/**. Export/members uses isAdmin + withTenantScope (app/api/admin/export/members/route.ts:26-50). Members API is in verify-high-risk-tenant-routes.cjs. The HTML /admin/members page (app/admin/members/page.tsx:38-60) uses global isAdmin and MEMBER_OR_DOGFOOD_WHERE with no organizationId — emails, phones, WIOA flags for every org. Same split: /admin/placements vs /api/admin/placements, /admin/training-progress vs /api/admin/training-progress. Staff use the SSR page. CI tenant grep never opens page.tsx list loaders.
evidence: app/admin/members/page.tsx:38 isAdmin; rg organizationId → no matches. app/api/admin/export/members/route.ts:26-50 isAdmin + getActorOrganizationId + withTenantScope. app/admin/placements/page.tsx:64-72 unscoped findMany take 500 including user.email. scripts/verify-high-risk-tenant-routes.cjs:33-37 checks members/route.ts not members/page.tsx. app/admin/layout.tsx:35 isAdmin not isAdminInOrg.

title: GDPR delete anonymizes users/profiles but leaves resume blobs and messages
blast: POST /api/gdpr/delete re-auths with password, signOut, raw UPDATE users email/name, UPDATE profiles nulls PII columns, inserts member_events, deletes Supabase auth user. It does not remove member-resumes / member-files objects (upload routes write cert-files/${userId}/ and resume paths). It does not delete or anonymize messages, applications.notes, placement_surveys, webhook payloads, or xapi_statements. Export (buildMemberExport) returns those tables — delete does not. lib/gdpr/ has no storage cleanup. Resume path columns are nulled so the app loses the pointer; the bucket object remains.
evidence: app/api/gdpr/delete/route.ts:75-119 raw SQL users+profiles+member_events only. rg storage|resume_original|member-resumes lib/gdpr → no matches. app/api/member/resume/upload/route.ts:48 uploads to BUCKET. app/api/member/certifications/upload/route.ts:8 BUCKET=member-files path cert-files/${user.id}. lib/member/exportData.ts:23-63 still lists applications, messages, placements, surveys.

title: Super-admin employer/partner impersonation cookies are unsigned UUIDs
blast: wa_super_admin_employer_id / wa_super_admin_partner_id are httpOnly, SameSite=lax, 7-day maxAge, value = raw employer/partner UUID. MFA trust cookies are HMAC'd with AUTH_TRUST_COOKIE_SECRET. A XSS or cookie-injection on a super-admin browser can retarget the portal to any employer id without hitting the POST setter. Setter does require isSuperAdmin; reader getEmployerForUser trusts the cookie if the user is already super_admin.
evidence: app/api/admin/employer-context/route.ts:16-22, :75 store.set(SUPER_ADMIN_EMPLOYER_COOKIE, employer.id). lib/auth/roles.ts:429-435 reads cookie then prisma.employer.findFirst({id}). lib/auth/mfaTrust.ts:15-20 throws without AUTH_TRUST_COOKIE_SECRET; :53-57 HMAC sign.

title: Production CSP still allows script-src unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval
blast: next.config.ts documents this as known (Next + GTM + Vercel Insights). Combined with hardcoded GTM-53JCT6WN in app/layout.tsx:56 it means any XSS in marketing HTML becomes script execution. Not a new hole; it is the remaining browser-control gap the first beat never recorded. frame-ancestors none and HSTS are set.
evidence: next.config.ts:60-77 CSP comment + script-src 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval' blob: GTM. app/layout.tsx:56 GTM_ID default GTM-53JCT6WN. Permissions-Policy camera=(self) microphone=(self) for interview video.
